title: Warm-side temperature slopes were more negative for six-month Pacific warm water volume change in 1980-2024 fits
abstract: We tested whether Pacific warm water volume change had equal slopes for positive and negative Nino 3.4 temperature anomalies. We used monthly PMEL GODAS and CPC ERSSTv5 snapshots. A continuous two-slope fit controlled for starting volume, calendar month and time. In 534 monthly starts in 1980-2024, the warm-minus-cold slope difference was -1.23 in units of 10^14 cubic metres per degree C. Its 95% three-year block interval was -1.86 to -0.58. Five-year blocks, no time trend, two time subsets, shorter and longer change windows, and removal of eight large warm-event years retained a negative interval. This is a conditional association in revised ocean products. It does not measure a causal heat loss rate, prove a physical mechanism, or establish forecast skill. The package contains raw snapshots, source hashes, monthly evidence, code, block draws, an independent numerical audit and a figure.

display.caption: Adjusted six-month volume change and warm-minus-cold slope contrasts. Lines in panel B are marginal 95% block intervals. Window lengths differ across two checks; compare signs rather than rates.
